says: leakgrep's --commits scans grafted history when the range's base is past a shallow boundary: in a shallow clone, the commits beyond the boundary are listed as the branch's own, and each grafted commit is read as a first commit, all it holds.
proof: In two cloud sessions (shallow clones) on 2026-11-18, `sh .agents/skills/lead/scripts/leakgrep.sh --commits origin/main..HEAD` reported 2,587 hits on two branches whose own 408 and 139 commits read clean from their real merge base; every hit was in old main history already on main. leakgrep.sh:214 hands the range to `git rev-list --reverse --parents` as given, and rev-list in a shallow clone stops at the grafted commits, which it lists with no parents.
cost: Every leak check run from a cloud session on a branch older than the clone's depth fails with thousands of false hits, so it cannot gate a push or a merge there, and a lead is tempted to read past it.
